planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in moist, well-drained soil in part shade to full sun; this robust botanical variety is noticeably larger in every part than typical Japanese beautyberry, so give it more room than the species type.

directions: Plant in moist but well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; var. luxurians is a robust, large-growing form of Japanese beautyberry with broader, coarser leaves and gracefully arching branches that carry noticeably larger clusters of deep lavender-purple berries than the straight species. Its scale and heavier fruit display make it a strong choice as a specimen or informal hedge where a bigger presence is wanted, similar in effect to Callicarpa bodinieri 'Profusion' but with an even more pendulous branch habit. Avoid overly alkaline soils, which can cause the foliage to yellow. Renewal-prune older stems in late winter to encourage vigorous new growth, since fruit is produced on the current season's wood.
